column2: Why can systemic vascular resistance alone not describe ventricular load?
column3: Resistance only relates mean pressure to mean flow, while the circulation is pulsatile; impedance also includes arterial compliance, blood inertia, wave reflection and frequency.

column2: How is organ perfusion pressure defined, and what is the relevant opposing pressure for the brain and for the left ventricle?

column2: How do unstressed and stressed volume differ, and what does venoconstriction do to them?
column3: Unstressed volume fills vessels without generating much pressure while stressed volume stretches the system and drives venous return; venoconstriction shifts volume into the stressed compartment, raising mean systemic filling pressure without added fluid.

column2: How do spontaneous inspiration and positive intrathoracic pressure differ in their effect on venous return?
